name: Sapporo
summary: Hokkaido's capital is a grid of wide streets built for snow. Eat your way through ramen, crab and soup curry, and add a day trip to the canal town of Otaru.
seasonNote: The Snow Festival in early February is the peak; summer is cool and dry while the rest of Japan swelters.
arrival: Rapid trains run from New Chitose Airport to Sapporo Station in about 40 minutes.
gettingAround: Three subway lines and a streetcar loop cover the centre; underground walkways link Sapporo Station to Susukino in winter.
cashTip: IC cards and credit cards work widely; small ramen counters use cash ticket machines.
foodTip: Try miso ramen, soup curry, jingisukan grilled lamb, fresh crab and soft-serve ice cream.
buyTip: Shiroi Koibito biscuits, Royce chocolate and Hokkaido dairy sweets.

connections.note: One of the world's busiest air routes; add transfers at both ends.

items.name: Odori Park and Sapporo TV Tower
items.summary: A 1.5 km strip of park through the city centre, home to the Snow Festival, with a tower viewpoint at one end.
items.expect: Snow sculptures in February and beer gardens in summer.
items.tip: Go up the TV Tower at dusk to see the park lit along its length.

items.summary: A 531-metre summit reached by ropeway and mini cable car, with a night view of the whole city.
items.expect: Cold and windy at the top; queues at sunset.
items.tip: Go up just before dusk and stay for the lights.

items.expect: Tour groups on the canal at midday.
items.tip: Sit on the right side of the train for sea views and stay until the gas lamps come on.
